correctness.rationale: Canonical half-digit representation, prime-square binomial congruence, exact nontrivial character products, and roots-of-unity inversion prove all q odd prime, all m≥1, all r. Endpoint sums A=1−m and W=m were recomputed; equality and branch boundary q|2m−1 were checked. Integer dynamic programming tested six primes × 25 lengths × every residue; direct integer enumeration tested q=3,5,7 through m=4. Finite tests do not establish the theorem, which follows from the symbolic proof.

evidence: Banks–Hart–Sakata (2004), arXiv:math/0405056v1, Lemma 3.1 writes general palindrome exponential sums as digit-sum products.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general factorization is a tool for proving, rather than an evaluation of, the quotient spectrum. Asymptotic uniformity for moduli coprime to b(b²−1) does not imply finite exact counts at this excluded modulus. No examined stronger theorem dominates the claimed two-level formula.

value.rationale: The modulus q=b+1 is forced in every even-length base-b palindrome; q² is the first meaningful refinement beyond trivial forced divisibility. The statement gives a complete exact all-residue classification, identifies one or two exceptional classes and precisely quantifies nonuniformity for every finite length. It supplies an explicit natural q-adic invariant, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice or a table recomputation.
